nodes.summary: Given a list $F$ of finite sets, a finite set $U$ and a rational cost $w(S)$ for each finite set $S$, this is the first set $S$ in $F$ with $S \cap U \ne \emptyset$ that minimizes the ratio $w(S) / |S \cap U|$ among the sets of $F$ meeting $U$, or nothing when no set of $F$ meets $U$.
nodes.title: Set with the least cost per new element

nodes.summary: Given a list $F$ of finite sets and a finite set $U$, the best set of $F$ for $U$ is the first set $S$ in the list $F$ that maximizes $|S \cap U|$, or $\emptyset$ when $F$ is empty.
nodes.title: Greedy choice of a set

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of finite sets and $T$ a finite set such that every element of $T$ lies in some member of $L$. Then $|T| \le \sum_{S \in L} |S \cap T|$, where the sum runs over the list $L$ with repetitions.
nodes.title: Covering bound by intersections

nodes.summary: Write $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ for the $n$-th harmonic number, so $H(0) = 0$. For natural numbers $d \le a \le k$, we have $\frac{d}{k} \le H(a) - H(a - d)$, where $\frac{d}{k}$ is read as $0$ when $k = 0$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for a difference of harmonic numbers

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set, and $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ the $n$-th harmonic number. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|C^*| \cdot H(|U|)$, where $|C^*|$ is the length of $C^*$.
nodes.title: Harmonic bound in the universe size for greedy set cover

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|C^*| \cdot (\ln |U| + 1)$, where $|C^*|$ is the length of $C^*$ and $\ln 0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Greedy set cover is a logarithmic approximation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets each with at most $d$ elements, $U$ a finite set, and $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ the $n$-th harmonic number. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|C^*| \cdot H(d)$, where $|C^*|$ is the length of $C^*$.
nodes.title: Harmonic bound in the largest set size for greedy set cover

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set such that every element of $U$ lies in some set of $F$. Then every element of $U$ lies in some set of the list returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$.
nodes.title: The greedy set cover is a cover

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set, and $H(n) = 1 + \frac12 + \dots + \frac1n$ the $n$-th harmonic number. For every list $C^*$ of members of $F$ that together cover $U$, the list of sets returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $\sum_{S \in C^*} H(|S \cap U|)$, where the sum runs over the list $C^*$ with repetitions.
nodes.title: Potential bound for greedy set cover

nodes.summary: For every list $F$ of finite sets and every finite set $U$, the list returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ has length at most $|U|$.
nodes.title: The greedy set cover has at most as many sets as elements

nodes.summary: For every list $F$ of finite sets and every finite set $U$, every set in the list returned by the greedy set cover algorithm on $F$ and $U$ is a member of $F$.
nodes.title: The greedy set cover draws its sets from the family

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set. The running time of greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ is at most $(|U| + 1)(|F| + \sum_{S \in F} |S|)$, where $|F|$ is the length of the list and the sum runs over the entries of $F$, counted with repetition.
nodes.title: Running time of greedy set cover

nodes.summary: Let $F = [S_1, \dots, S_n]$ be a list of finite sets and $U$ a finite set. The greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ is computed as follows. Let $T$ be the first $S_i$ in the list that maximizes $|S_i \cap U|$, or $T = \emptyset$ when $n = 0$. If $T \cap U = \emptyset$, the result is the empty list; otherwise it is $T$ followed by the greedy set cover of $U \setminus T$ from $F$. Each step, including the last one, costs…
nodes.title: Greedy set cover

nodes.summary: For a function $w$ assigning a rational cost to each finite set, the total cost of a list $C = [S_1, \dots, S_m]$ of finite sets is $w(S_1) + \dots + w(S_m)$, a set that occurs several times in $C$ being counted each time.
nodes.title: Total cost of a list of sets

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set, $w$ a rational cost function on finite sets with $w(S) \ge 0$ for every $S$ in $F$, and $d$ a natural number such that every set in $F$ has at most $d$ elements. If $C^*$ is a list of sets from $F$ whose union contains $U$, then the weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$ has total cost at most $H(d)$ times the total cost of $C^*$, where…
nodes.title: Chvátal's bound

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set and $w$ a rational cost function on finite sets with $w(S) \ge 0$ for every $S$ in $F$. If $C^*$ is a list of sets from $F$ whose union contains $U$, then the weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$ has total cost at most $\sum_{S \in C^*} w(S)\, H(|S \cap U|)$, the sum running over the entries of $C^*$ with repetition, where…
nodes.title: Potential bound for weighted greedy set cover

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set and $w$ any rational cost function on finite sets. If every element of $U$ lies in some set of $F$, then every element of $U$ lies in some set chosen by the weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$.
nodes.title: The weighted greedy set cover is a cover

nodes.summary: For every list $F$ of finite sets, finite set $U$ and rational cost function $w$ on finite sets, every set chosen by the weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$ belongs to $F$.
nodes.title: The weighted greedy set cover uses sets of the family

nodes.summary: Let $F = [S_1, \dots, S_m]$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set and $w$ a rational cost function on finite sets. The weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$ runs in time at most $(|U| + 1)\,(m + |S_1| + \dots + |S_m|)$: at most $|U| + 1$ searches for a best set, each costing $m$ plus the total size of the sets of $F$.
nodes.title: Running time of weighted greedy set cover

nodes.summary: Let $F = [S_1, \dots, S_n]$ be a list of finite sets, $U$ a finite set and $w$ a function giving each finite set $S$ a rational cost $w(S)$. The weighted greedy set cover of $U$ from $F$ with costs $w$ is computed as follows. If no $S_i$ meets $U$, the result is the empty list. Otherwise let $T$ be the first $S_i$ in the list with $S_i \cap U \ne \emptyset$ that minimizes $w(S_i) / |S_i \cap U|$ among the sets of…
nodes.title: Weighted greedy set cover

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
